chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about weakness, so it was said to him: 'Cook the meat with the milk, for these two strengthen the body.' He said: 'Is it Al-Muzeyra?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the meat with the milk of the udder (fresh milk/yoghurt milk).'
ai.seo_question: What did Allah instruct a Prophet to cook to strengthen his body against weakness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic tradition of dietary medicine, where Allah prescribed a nutrient-dense combination of meat and fresh milk to combat physical weakness. The Imam’s clarification distinguishes the beneficial fresh milk (*al-haleeb*) from fermented curds (*al-muzeyra*), reflecting Shia scholarly emphasis on precise textual interpretation in matters of health and nutrition. This narrative underscores the holistic view of the body in Shia tradition, where physical strength is seen as a trust requiring proper nourishment.
